harnesses.rationale: Baseline harness: no learned rules, no guardrails, all tools.
systemRules: Complete the task using the available tools, then reply DONE.

harnesses.rationale: A single general rule requiring run_tests after any write, plus a fix-and-rerun loop, directly targets the largest cluster at no tool or safety cost. Adding a skill distilled from the passing conv trails adds a reusable procedure (inspect docs and conventions, write, verify, iterate) that also helps the convention tasks. Enabling retrieveK lets stored lessons reach the worker. These are small changes with no guardrail risk.

skills.title: Inspect, write, verify with run_tests, iterate on failure
skills.body:
1. Read the input files the task names. If a directory is involved, list_files it and read any README or docs it points to (e.g. a style guide) for format conventions.
2. Produce the output exactly as the task and conventions require: correct path, ordering, separators, trailing newline and schema fields.
3. Call run_tests immediately after writing.
4. On FAIL, read the failure message carefully (expected vs actual, ordering, missing fields), rewrite the file, and call run_tests again.
5. Reply DONE only after tests have run, ideally passing. Budget turns so that at least one write→test→fix cycle fits.

systemRules: Complete the task using the available tools, then reply DONE.

After creating or modifying any file, always call run_tests before replying DONE. If tests fail, read the failure output, fix the files, and rerun run_tests until they pass or turns run out. Never reply DONE without having run tests at least once.

generations.diagnosis: The largest failure cluster is skipped_verification, with 4 failures, all in the verify family. In each case the worker read config/servers.json, wrote out/hosts.txt and declared DONE after 3 turns without ever calling run_tests. The outputs may also be wrong: the order or format of the hostnames is unverified, so running tests would expose any mismatch. The passing convention trails show the working pattern: read the relevant docs, write the file, run run_tests, fix the file on FAIL and rerun. maxTurns=8 leaves enough budget for that loop.
lessons: Always call run_tests after writing output files and before replying DONE; tasks fail as skipped_verification even when the output looks right.
When extracting a list from a config file (e.g. hostnames), check the tests or docs for the required order and format; run_tests failures reveal expected vs actual.
Reserve turns for a write→run_tests→fix loop; don't stop after the first write.
